title: CRASH-084: putenv empty key string freed via hash del still in environ uaf (use-after-free)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free at ext/standard/basic_functions.c:1381 in zif_putenv when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 336b5f59b6c4, which postdates the release, and names the defect at ext/standard/basic_functions.c:1381 (UAF read); enabling missing guard at ext/standard/basic_functions.c:1333, free at 1376 -> php_putenv_destructor:922
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing.
fault_sites_why: ASan's access stack in our native run (results-ours-asan-default.json, sha256 045e3366bfc5) has zif_putenv at ext/standard/basic_functions.c:1381 as its first frame inside PHP's tree (frame #0); the stack's remaining frames are the interpreter's dispatch and are not sites

status: built 2026-10-27 from the corpus and our native oracle; what has run is in this record's arms (verdict, verdict_from) and under results/
note: population: asan-blind -- ASan reports it only with PHP's allocator patched (cache off, no 8-byte rounding); with zend_alloc.c as shipped the run reads OK. That is the selection, by measurement; which mechanism hides it, and which arm sees it, is what the arms record. Collected by the corpus as history-5x-stdext (historical-known, confidence high).

platform_precondition.needs: putenv keeps an empty-name string referenced from environ

platform_precondition_why: musl 1.2.5's putenv (src/env/putenv.c) takes the unsetenv branch for an empty name -- `if (!l || !s[l]) return unsetenv(s);` -- and unsetenv refuses a name containing '=' with EINVAL, so the string is never stored in environ. The use-after-free this case records needs that stored reference: the second empty-name putenv frees the string and the following environ scan reads it (the corpus's native oracle, glibc). Without the reference there is nothing dangling, so a run that completes on this libc is not a miss of the protection; it is a defect whose precondition this platform does not meet. Checked, not asserted: ports/php/app/probe-putenv.c runs on every arm and says what this libc retains, with a control that proves it can see retention at all.
